proof_summary: A finite cotangent Fourier identity expresses the difference between the negative-residue mirror sum and the original sum as a divisor sum of local cotangent-weighted imaginary quadratic Gauss sums. Explicit Gauss-sum evaluations reduce each local term to zero or a nonnegative multiple of an odd real character cotangent sum, whose positivity follows from the Euler product for its Dirichlet series and passage to \(s=1\); hence the original sum is at most its mirror, and pairing every residue with its negative gives \(2a(n)\le n(n-1)\le n^2-1\).
